critique.evidence: Strong cyber-editorial identity, restrained cyan/red palette, bold headline, and consistent mono labeling create clear hierarchy across viewports. However, the desktop atlas visibly clips the leftmost vector column and its headings, the dense five-column grid becomes cramped, and the inspector/code block feels visually under-resolved. Tablet and mobile reflow more cleanly, but the very tall composition, tiny low-contrast metadata, truncated code, and horizontally clipped global navigation reduce polish. Mobile also loses the brand name, weakening header balance and continuity.
critique.fix: Eliminate desktop column clipping and give the grid more breathing room; constrain or wrap code content; raise metadata contrast and minimum type size; tighten the long tablet/mobile vertical rhythm; and redesign the compact header so the brand and current location remain visible without relying on clipped horizontal navigation.
